Definition: Assuming a supernatural cause merely because no natural explanation is at hand. A gap in knowledge is not evidence for any particular cause, and it must not be confused with positive arguments from evidence.
Example: Someone argues, 'Science can't explain this yet, so it must be a miracle.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'No one can explain this healing, so it proves this doctrine' — the gap alone proves no doctrine.
HowToRespond: Ask for positive reasons: "A gap in our knowledge isn't evidence for any particular cause — let's look for positive reasons."
